newsitem.title: USA: First lady Hillary Clinton gets Grammy nomination.
newsitem.headline: First lady Hillary Clinton gets Grammy nomination.

text.p: First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton received a Grammy nomination on Tuesday for the audio version of her best-selling book "It Takes a Village," organisers announced.
Clinton will be up against several Hollywood celebrities in the spoken word or non-musical album category.

The other nominees in the catedgory include Lauren Bacall, Martin Landau, Jack Lemmon and Gregory Peck for their work on the Paul Werth book, "Harry S. Truman: A Journey to Independence." Also nominated were Ed Asner, Ellen Burstyn, CCH Pounder and Alfre Woodard in "Grow Old Along With Me -- The Best Is Yet To Come."

Radio humorist and commentator Garrison Keilor's reading of Mark Twain's "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" and CBS newsman Charles Kuralt's narration of his own "Charles Kuralt's America" rounded out the list.
The winner will be announced on Feb. 26 at the 39th annual Grammy Awards ceremony at New York' Madison Square Garden.
